conflicts.issue: Creating a dedicated organization is one scenario architecture, not authority to create or restructure the user's estate. Existing function-owned polyrepo consumers and canonical standard repository remain.
The example calls a six-character commit reference immutable and shows mutable version tags; full-commit pinning policy requires stronger references, with reviewed updates.
Internal visibility is not complete evidence of private workflow consumption, permissions, cross-organization access or effective security.
A weekly update schedule, sample security-team account and sample secret token do not establish correct consumer configuration.
Claimed40percent configuration savings and30to50percent duplication reduction are unsupported local measurements.
Telemetry, leaderboards and mandatory adoption can conflict with privacy, capacity and behavior incentives; approval and outcome-focused measures are required.
Centralization and federation are deliberate alternatives. Security coordination does not require uniform repositories, languages or rollout without exceptions.
